newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin vows Russian government reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin vows Russian government reshuffle.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin vowed on Thursday to reshuffle Russia's government and singled out the Finance Ministry for criticism.
His comments at a cabinet meeting fuelled speculation that Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, attacked by Chernomyrdin on Wednesday, would lose his job in the forthcoming reshuffle.

"The time has come to concentrate on the most essential questions -- to change the style of the government's work, its structure and personal composition. We will act decisively and systematically," the premier said.

Chernomyrdin was echoing President Boris Yeltsin, who earlier told parliament that the composition and structure of the government would be changed and new appointments would be announced in the next few days.
Neither Yeltsin nor Chernomyrdin said who would be involved in the changes.
But Chernomyrdin said the Finance Ministry should not be the dominant body in economic policy and the role of the Economy Ministry in this area should be strengthened.
"The Economy Ministry should be the headquarters of the country's economic policy," he told a cabinet meeting.
"Here is where the conception of the budget and the development of federal programmes will begin."
Chernomyrdin said the Economy Ministry should not be less powerful than the Finance Ministry, which was displaying excessive bureaucracy and arrogance towards the regions and other ministries.

Kremlin sources say Yeltsin's chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais could return to the cabinet as first deputy prime minister with a broad role supervising the economy and combatting economic crime and corruption.
But earlier on Thursday Chubais said Yeltsin had not yet decided whether to transfer him to the government.
